entries.reason: CMTag arrived at iOS 17 and the SDK the toolchain resolves is 16.4, where no CoreMedia header has Tag in its name; 26.2's CMTag.h declares this one CM_INLINE, so the package's header carries the body - the port's own body, written from the measurement below and not transcribed from Apple's, with its provenance in the comment above it. Header text is otherwise used only as facts: the name, the signature, the types
entries.effect: true when the two tags share a category, whatever their data types and values are - measured: two tags sharing a category and differing in BOTH data type and value still compare equal, and a category taken from a third tag is false
entries.source: the host's own CoreMedia, in C, over 672 answers: every data type, INT32_MAX and INT32_MIN+1 categories, a float's bit pattern, both zeros, a NaN, an infinity, an SInt64 -1 and an unsigned all-ones, and all 16x16 tag pairs for the two that compare two tags. The probe is tests/backports/host/coremedia7/cmtaginlines.m and it yields the HOST's answers. It does not exercise the port's own text and no check does: the host SDK's <CoreMedia/CoreMedia.h> includes Apple's <CoreMedia/CMTag.h> at its line 19, so on this host the port's bodies are shadowed before they are compiled, and a two-table comparison here would compare Apple's inlines with Apple's. The port's bodies are the definitions on an SDK with no CMTag.h, which is the 16.4 SDK the port targets - measured by compiling the probe for armv7-apple-ios6.0 against it - and that is where they take effect

entries.effect: CONSISTENT, AND NOT THE HOST'S VALUE. Equal tags hash equal and the six measured tags do not collide, so it is a usable hash of a tag. It is not the host's mixing: the host's six are 242338807774, 930912231118, 175247075667, 175254150787, 175196967445 and 175247284034, all inside a ~40-bit band, and nine candidates were evaluated in C against the host - the category, data type and low or high 32 bits of the value XORed together, multiply-and-mix by 31 and by 33, FNV-1a 32 and 64 over the struct's 16 bytes, CFHash of a dictionary of the three fields as CFNumbers, and CFHash of a CFNumber of the value. None reproduces the host's values, and the self-check rejects four of the nine before comparison because they cannot tell two of the six apart - the two XOR forms that fold the value's low half, CFHash of the dictionary (a constant 3, the dictionary's own hash) and CFHash of the number (0 for both zero values). The table is facts/CoreMedia/cmtag-fixtures/hashfit.txt and the program that produced it is beside it; the host's mixing is not identified, and the gap is recorded in coordination/crutches.md
entries.source: the host's own CoreMedia, measured in C by facts/CoreMedia/cmtag-fixtures/hashfit.m, which is built against the host SDK because CFHash does not exist in Python and every candidate that involves it has to run against the real CFHash
